personality: Silver-tongued, ingenious and ruthless. The finest teller of tales in Gwynedd, and a great liar.
voice: Lord, I know where they are.

cards.title: The Swine of Dyved
cards.text: Gwydion, nephew of Math, was the best storyteller in the world. To win wondrous pigs from the court of Dyved, he went there disguised as a bard, charmed the king with tales, and traded for the swine with horses and hounds of his own making that faded away the next day. It started a war.

source.author: medieval Welsh tales; English by Lady Charlotte Guest, 1838–49
source.edition: Project Gutenberg text of Guest's translation

cards.title: Three Years as Beasts
cards.text: For that and for a worse crime, Math struck Gwydion and his brother with his magic wand. For a year they ran as deer, the next as wild swine, the next as wolves, and each year they came back with a young one born to them. Only after three years did Math give them back their own shapes.

source.author: medieval Welsh tales; English by Lady Charlotte Guest, 1838–49

cards.title: The Eagle on the Oak
cards.text: When Llew was struck down and flew away as an eagle, Gwydion searched all Gwynedd for him. He followed a sow to an oak, and high in its branches sat a wasted eagle. Gwydion sang to it until it came down to his knee, then struck it with his wand, and Llew stood there again, nothing but skin and bone.
